evals.prompt: I just started this app in Lovable. It is not live. I have never used Sentry. Nothing in the code catches errors. What should I do?
evals.expected_output: Names the stage as uncaught errors and explains error checking in plain language, including why it is worth doing. Does not recommend milestones, dashboards, or Seer. Does not install Sentry.
assertions: Names uncaught errors as the stage
Explains error checking in plain language
Does not recommend milestones, dashboards, or Seer
Does not look for a code-driven dashboard
Does not install Sentry

evals.prompt: The app is live. Errors are caught at one handler. We log extra context around those errors and sample them. Sourcemaps are sent. I cannot tell if login is working.
evals.expected_output: Says the next stage is a milestone, such as login, because the app is live and that is how you know the lights are on. Does not jump to Seer.
assertions: Says the next stage is a milestone
Uses login as the example of the lights being on
Does not jump to Seer
Does not look for a code-driven dashboard

evals.prompt: Does our GitHub Action send the sourcemap to Sentry?
evals.expected_output: Uses the github skill for that look. Does not re-walk the other GitHub looks.
assertions: Uses the github skill
Does not re-walk the other GitHub looks

evals.prompt: We catch errors, log with sampling, send sourcemaps, record a login milestone, and have a dashboard of those events. Are we mature? A non-technical co-founder wants to know why any of this matters.
evals.expected_output: Says the project is mature because both sides exist: errors can be addressed, and milestones show what is working. Tells that in a story a non-technical person can follow. Names Seer as the top of the score and does not turn it on. Events, logs, milestones, and sourcemaps are present, and no dashboard file is in the repo, so names a code-driven dashboard as a nice-to-have and does not treat it as a maturity gap.
assertions: Says the project is mature because both sides exist
Tells the story for a non-technical person
Names Seer as the top of the score
Does not turn Seer on
Names a code-driven dashboard as a nice-to-have
Does not treat the missing file as a maturity gap

evals.prompt: mcp.json names a sentry server. I cannot see anything calling it. Can we go deeper on sentry?
evals.expected_output: Says the MCP setup is there. Says use is unseen. Does not say they can go deeper. Does not print a URL or a token. Does not add the server.
assertions: Says the MCP setup is there
Says use is unseen
Does not say they can go deeper
Does not print a URL or a token
Does not add the server

evals.prompt: mcp.json names a sentry server, and the project config shows that server is enabled and called. Can we go deeper?
evals.expected_output: Says the Sentry MCP is used. Says they can go deeper. Does not call it. Does not print a URL or a token.
assertions: Says the Sentry MCP is used
Says they can go deeper
Does not call it
Does not print a URL or a token
